importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation is extreme — tabletop shelf units, walk-in polycarbonate structures, dome polyfilm greenhouses, and decorative glass terrariums are completely distinct products. Buyers use the image to identify product type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Covering material (polycarbonate vs. polyfilm vs. shade net), frame material, and size are non-interchangeable primary shortlisting criteria. Buyers arrive with a specific application and footprint constraint; listings without these specs cannot be evaluated.

Price varies substantially across covering material and size tiers — polycarbonate walk-in units command a significant premium over polyfilm or tabletop units. Indian buyers compare prices after confirming type fit; listed price is a budget entry point before negotiation.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall exists in the Indian mini greenhouse market — the market is fragmented across regional fabricators and buyers search by spec and size, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Seller credibility matters for assembly support, installation guidance, and warranty fulfilment, particularly for first-time buyers. No brand-dominant sibling MCATs exist and buyers evaluate seller ratings rather than brand identity.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Larger custom structures may be quoted per square metre but this is uncommon for the primary B2B segment on IndiaMART; tabletop units are per piece — all are implied and never a buyer question.
importance_ranking.reason: Mini greenhouses are sold as complete prefabricated kits and the per-unit basis is entirely implied. No buyer questions whether a greenhouse kit is sold per piece.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Polycarbonate vs. polyfilm vs. shade net are non-interchangeable covering types with a significant price delta — polycarbonate units command a substantial premium over polyfilm — and define the product's durability tier and UV protection level.

Walk-in vs. tabletop vs. wall-mounted are completely different product classes serving different buyer needs and footprint constraints, with a large price delta between sub-types — a buyer cannot substitute one for another.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Buyers have a specific terrace or balcony footprint constraint and size is the first filter — sellers need dimensions to confirm their product range is relevant and to quote accurately.

Natural vs. fan-assisted vs. exhaust-fan ventilation is a key functional differentiator that affects crop health and price — buyers in hot climates specifically require active ventilation and sellers need this to confirm product fit.

top_rfq_specs.reason: GI, MS, PVC, and aluminium frames represent different durability and price tiers — sellers specialise in specific frame types and need this to confirm product fit and quote accurately.

UV stabilised film, shade net, polycarbonate, and FRP are non-interchangeable covering types that define the product's functional tier — sellers need this to identify the correct product line and price point.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Buyers have a specific footprint constraint (terrace or balcony area) and size determines whether the seller's product range is relevant — without this, sellers cannot confirm fit or quote accurately.

Walk-in, tabletop, and dome are completely different product classes — sellers manufacturing walk-in structures cannot supply tabletop units, making this the primary routing spec for accurate seller matching.
